title: GTA 6 Changes the Run Button After 25 Years
description: After nearly 25 years of tradition, GTA 6 is finally ditching the classic face button tapping mechanic required to make your character run.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## A Quarter-Century Tradition Comes to an End

For nearly 25 years, the Grand Theft Auto series has maintained a very specific and iconic control scheme when it comes to getting around on foot. In almost every major installment, moving your character at a sprint has uniquely required mapping your movement to a face button on a controller. No matter which platform you preferred, the default experience always meant repeatedly tapping X or A to get your character to truly peg it across the map.

While Rockstar Games has occasionally included alternate control schemes in some of their titles over the years, the classic default has stubbornly remained the same. Players have simply grown accustomed to the rhythmic tapping required just to travel efficiently in the virtual world.

## GTA 6 Bucks the Trend

According to recent reports from gaming media outlet Eurogamer, Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally bucking this long-standing trend. The upcoming title will no longer require players to tap a face button repeatedly in order to run. This marks a significant departure from mechanics that have defined the franchise since its early 3D era.

As the industry evolves, modern control conventions have increasingly favored smoother, less repetitive inputs for basic locomotion. Ditching the face-button tap for sprinting suggests a modernized approach to player movement and overall ergonomics in the highly anticipated sequel set in Leonida.

## Editor's Take

It might seem like a small quality-of-life update, but changing a fundamental input method used for 25 years is a bold and welcome step. Removing the repetitive button-mashing requirement for running shows that Rockstar is actively modernizing the core gameplay loop to match contemporary standards, ensuring a more comfortable and fluid open-world experience.
